title: Wills, Trusts and Estates
audience: a law student in a U.S. JD program
purpose: Analyze intestate succession, wills (execution, revocation, capacity, undue influence and interpretation), will substitutes, trusts (creation, kinds, trustee duties and modification), powers of appointment, spousal and family protection, and basic estate planning, using the Uniform Probate Code and the common law.
primary_reading: Uniform Law Commission: the Uniform Probate Code and Uniform Trust Code

weeks.8: The spousal elective share and omitted heirs
weeks.12: Powers of appointment and estate-planning basics

blocks.deliverable: Distribute five intestate estates under the Uniform Probate Code.
Decide whether a will was validly executed and later revoked.
Apply an anti-lapse statute to three gifts.
Week 7 midterm; compute a surviving spouse's elective share.
Decide whether a valid trust was created.
Analyze a trustee's breach of the duty of loyalty.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Estate plan: for a supplied family, compute the intestate shares, then outline a will and revocable trust that meet their goals, with a memo explaining each choice.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
